headline: Scott Kupor, vice chair of the White House's Super Intelligence Force, says the AI task force will press companies to test products before release and will check their safety claims itself.
score_reason: Lowered from the pool score of 5: the interview was on 12 Oct 2026, before today's window, and repeats themes of his 10 Oct Fox News remarks; the new points are independent checks and audits, which are only ideas under study.
importance_line: AI companies, which may face government checks on their safety claims, and the public who depend on those claims are affected, but Kupor described ideas the task force is considering, not rules, and did not say whether developers or data centre operators will face new legal requirements.
summary: MeriTalk reports that Scott Kupor, vice chair of the White House Super Intelligence Force and director of the Office of Personnel Management, said in a CNBC interview on 12 Oct 2026 that the AI task force, announced on 4 Oct 2026, will not wait for companies to say they have done their safety work, and is weighing independent audits whose findings go to company boards while the government keeps the power to verify and enforce. He also said slowing AI down would not stop adversaries advancing and urged companies to deal with data centres' electricity and water demands, and our 11 Oct 2026 edition carried his earlier remarks on Fox News.
notes: POLITICO page gave HTTP 403; the same story was read at MeriTalk (reporting the 12 Oct CNBC interview; the CNBC page was also blocked). POLITICO's own event date is unconfirmed. The score is lowered by 1 because the event was on 12 Oct; the 12 Oct edition ended at 08:12 UTC and the CNBC interview went out at 11:32 UTC, so it fell in the gap between editions and the editor may restore 5.
